claim_b: CJ (2024): a Hungarian plant will supply bibigo dumplings to Europe from H2 2026; bibigo vegetable dumplings at Coles are made in Australia (XBA-23; XBA-25)
position_taken: Vietnam's role in CJ's Western supply is partial and may shrink for Europe (inferred)
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). Not a contradiction in fact; a change of plan over time.

claim_a: 63.7 plus or minus 11.7 on the 0.5 to 3 year pattern, in vivo, two datasets; PDCAAS 78.9 (NQR-05)
claim_b: 98 on the older-child pattern and 84 on the young-child pattern, in vitro INFOGEST (NQR-09)
position_taken: Use both ends (64 to 98) for cost adjustment and do not average; the older-child value applies to schoolchildren but rests on an in vitro method

claim_a: 12.96 g per 100 g (Decision 3958 Appendix 7, APR-04)
claim_b: 14.8 g per 100 g (FCT 2007 code 9001, DIE-12; used in the package price ladder)

topic: Protein a school lunch should supply, age 6 to 7
claim_a: 15.3 to 31.4 g: 30 to 40% of 1,570 kcal at 13 to 20% of energy from protein (Decision 3958 rule, APR-04; our calculation)
claim_b: 9.6 to 12.8 g: 30 to 40% of the 32 g a day in the NIN 2026 lookup (NQR-01)
position_taken: Use the RNI share for adequacy and note that the energy-share rule makes software menus protein-heavy
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). Explains why one Hanoi school's published lunch carries 31.8 g (PMR-26; our calculation).

claim_a: A soybean school meal added 0.5 cm in 8 months in Bangladesh (NQR-27); school milk improved height-for-age in rural Vietnam (NQR-25)
claim_b: Daily milk and egg for two years did not change height in rural China (NQR-26)
position_taken: Treat height gains at school age as small and uncertain; the stronger designs show none
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). NQR-27 had two clusters; NQR-25 allocation not stated in the abstract.

claim_a: Pig DIAAS 86 (SCI-41)
claim_b: Human ileal digestibility in children about 20% lower (SCI-42)
position_taken: Use 69 to 86 (our calculation for the low end)
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). Already logged in the package as DG-110; restated for this table.

topic: Zinc and iron values in the 2026 recommended intakes
claim_a: Decision 3958 cites the 2016 RNI for zinc and iron by age (APR-04)
claim_b: The NIN online lookup, updated in March 2026 after Decision 116/QD-VDD, shows identical zinc and iron values (NQR-01)
position_taken: Treat the values as current until Decision 116 is read
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). Either the 2026 revision kept them or the lookup mixes versions.

topic: Size and growth of food e-commerce
claim_a: About 1% of food retail value in 2024, growing 29% (Euromonitor via USDA, CHN-01)
claim_b: Grocery and food on four marketplaces VND 19.55 trillion in H1 2026, up 151% on H1 2025; about 2.7% of the 2024 food retail base if doubled for the year (ECR-02; our calculation)
position_taken: Both stand: different years and scopes. Use CHN-01 for 2024 and Metric for 2026, with the caveat that Metric does not publish its category definition or method
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). Metric implies about 1.1% for H1 2025 on the same base, which agrees with CHN-01; the gap is growth in 2026, not a conflict of measurement

topic: Whether protein content now sells plant milk
claim_a: Rising searches for high-protein nut milk and Vinamilk's Sua Hat Cao Dam are the first sign that protein content sells in this aisle (ch13; CON-37; BUY-16)
claim_b: On Kamereo the protein-claimed GoldSoy Giau Dam soy milk sold 2,609 units against 5,758 and 5,828 for unclaimed unsweetened soy milks priced higher (ECR-06)
position_taken: Keep the ch13 statement for consumer search and one product; add that the kitchen channel does not show it
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). Different buyers (households against kitchens), cumulative counters with unknown start dates, and a stock-out for GoldSoy: weak evidence either way

topic: Weight of Kamereo loose white tofu
claim_a: Piece weight not stated, so no price per kg (wave 7, CPC-12)
claim_b: The product description gives Size: 70 g per piece (ECR-06)
position_taken: Use 70 g: VND 84,857 per kg and about VND 77,900 per 100 g of protein on the FCT value (our calculation)
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). Same page; the size sits in the description field

topic: Retail price of Orgain Organic Protein 920 g
claim_a: VND 1,385,900 at a premium store in Thao Dien (FORM-01, P171)
claim_b: VND 1,150,000 at WheyShop (ECR-08)
position_taken: Both are real shelf prices; the premium-store figure is the top of the range
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). The package's protein-powder median (VND 71,900 per 20 g of protein) comes only from premium stores

topic: Price benchmark for a meat extender
claim_a: TPP-03 and ch14.4: the extender only has to cost the processor less than the lean meat it replaces
claim_b: TPP-06, ch16.7 and ch16.8: price fungal biomass against egg white and dairy proteins, never against soy
position_taken: Both are partly right, for different jobs. Lean is a ceiling that never binds. The binder job (1 to 3% of recipe) is priced against egg and milk protein; the extension job (10 to 30% of lean) against hydrated soy, about USD 2.5 to 2.7 per kg of protein
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). This line, sections 5 and 8

topic: How much meat a plant or fungal protein can replace
claim_a: TPP-03: 20 to 30% replacement, up to 50%; Singapore blind test: chicken mince with 30 to 50% plant protein beat 100% chicken (NOV-37; NOV-40)
claim_b: US frankfurter and sausage study: practical lean replacement below 30% (HXE-04); UK hybrids above 30% often failed (HXE-09; HXE-12); soy lowered acceptance of emulsified pork meatballs (HXE-08)
position_taken: For pork products: 10 to 20% in fine emulsions, up to 30% in coarse mince; 50% supported only in one coarse chicken mince test
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). Singapore result is a press-release summary of one product

topic: What a processor pays for lean pork
claim_a: TPP-03 uses retail lean at about VND 132,000 per kg (COST-39)
claim_b: Carcass-equivalent floor of 1.38 times live (about VND 81,000 at September 2026 prices); processors buy trimmings, not retail trays
position_taken: Model processor lean at 1.8 times live (about VND 105,000 at September 2026 prices), with 1.5 and 2.2 as bounds
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). No business-to-business price found

topic: Where soy sits in Vissan lines
claim_a: ch14.4 and ch16.3: added proteins sit mostly in value lines and cut meat cost
claim_b: Label prices: soy appears in the DHA nutrition sausage that has more lean (58% against 55%) and a higher price; the cheapest gio lua (VND 124,200 per kg) lists chicken and starch, not soy
position_taken: Soy is used for binding and protein in value and nutrition lines; the cheapest lines cut cost mainly with chicken, skin, starch and water
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). BUY-05 prices; our reading

topic: Whether extension is a hedge against pork price swings
claim_a: brief-manufacturers and ch11: an extender hedges pork price swings
claim_b: Model: 20% extension removes about a sixth of a recipe exposure to the 2019 to 2020 pork shock; the saving exists at every price
position_taken: Treat extension as a standing cost saving; the hedge effect is small
notes: Version 0.4 (wave8, actor check and expansion). Our calculation, section 6

topic: How often meat is found in Vietnamese chay
claim_a: Can Tho University kit paper: there have been many cases of meat detected in vegetarian foods through process failure or mixing [CHY-61]
claim_b: Press and enforcement record 2015 to 2026: no confirmed case; one 2021 seizure on suspicion with no published result [TRU-18; TRU-22; LBL-23; LBL-24]
position_taken: Frequency is unmeasured; treat fake chay as a latent rumour and screen for it cheaply within DMV-07
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). The CTU paper tested no market samples

topic: Whether soy protein is a positive or a negative
claim_a: Health media and suppliers: soy is 'boneless meat', 25 g a day recommended, a functional meat ingredient [TRU-22; TRU-23; TRU-28]
claim_b: Artisan sellers: 'no soy protein filler' as a quality claim [TRU-27]
position_taken: Both hold in different contexts: soy is positive as a food and neutral when listed in industrial sausages; negative when hidden, cost-driven or in products sold on purity
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Snippet evidence on the seller side

topic: Taiwanese fake-chay figures relayed in Vietnam
claim_a: VietNamNet 2015: 70% (15 of 21) of Taiwanese imitation-meat samples contained animal products [TRU-01]
claim_b: Same article: Taiwan FDA found labelled packs mostly compliant and 4 of 15 loose samples with pork or chicken [TRU-01]
position_taken: Do not use either figure for Vietnam; they show only that the story circulated
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Original Taiwanese sources not traced

topic: First fine-emulsion format for the TPP-03 test
claim_a: W8-L6: one fine emulsion, giò lụa or xúc xích, plus one coarse format
claim_b: This line: industrial xúc xích, not giò lụa, because giò lụa's public quality test is the absence of starch and 2019 extension was read as cheating [TRU-02; TRU-03; TRU-27]
position_taken: Xúc xích first; giò lụa only after a label test
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Texture limits in W8-L6 (HXE-01) point the same way

topic: Whether mixed-protein meat products carry a label penalty
claim_a: Part III ch14.4: mixed-protein products from the largest processors sell at mass scale without a label penalty [BUY-05]
claim_b: 2019: starch extension of market giò cost sellers customers and was called dishonest [TRU-03]
position_taken: Both hold: the penalty falls on hidden cost-cutting in artisan channels, not on listed soy in branded lines
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Different channels and disclosure

topic: Do upland border-commune and boarding lunches lack animal food, creating a zinc gap?
claim_a: W8-L4: border-commune lunches can afford protein but need zinc; a lunch with little animal protein doubles the zinc a kitchen must serve; TPP-11 targets Decree 339 kitchens [APR-09; APR-04]
claim_b: This line: 0 of 124 upland lunches were animal-free; Decree 339 lunches at one border school bought 107 to 179 g of raw pork a pupil; weighed boarding diets in Yen Bai met zinc at 131 to 157% [UPL-04; UPL-01 to UPL-17; UPL-18]
position_taken: Where menus are published, lunch zinc is met; the gap W8-L4 describes applies only to a dish that removes all meat, which kitchens do not serve. Keep W8-L4's zinc bands as the rule for any such product.
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Publication bias and plans versus plates are the main caveats; the under-five zinc deficiency (53.3%, 2020) is a different population

topic: How much animal protein do poor upland children get?
claim_a: Part III ch11.2: too little high-quality protein at very low cost in poor upland districts; stunting above 30% in the worst provinces [DIE-01; DIE-03]
claim_b: Boarding school plates are meat-heavy: pork was in 102 of 124 lunches (82%) in 13 schools (our register upland_school_weeks.csv) [UPL-01 to UPL-17]
position_taken: Both can hold: ch11.2 concerns under-fives and home diets, which this line does not measure; boarders eat most weekday meals at school
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Boarders are a subset of upland children; day pupils and preschool children are not covered

topic: Animals spared per canteen meal replaced
claim_a: W7-L3: about 0.020 at the national dish mix; about 1,090 animals per tonne of protein [FUF-03]
claim_b: Observed caterer menus: 0.015 (0.010 to 0.029); about 745 animals per tonne, because pork and beef take more and poultry less of the meat-led dishes [UPL-27 to UPL-32]
position_taken: Give both as a range; sample menus are marketing and mostly southern
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Neither counts fish, which leads 26% of canteen protein dishes

topic: Are upland meals thin or rich?
claim_a: Press and charity reports: rations cut at Hoang Thu Pho 1 (2022 to 2023); menus had two dishes before a VND 10,000 top-up; pupils skipped breakfast [UPL-24; UPL-25]
claim_b: Published menus and cost sheets: two main dishes and meat at almost every lunch and dinner [UPL-01 to UPL-17]
position_taken: Both: published menus describe the better-run schools and the plan; press describes failures and pre-2025 budgets. The Decree 66 increase (VND 936,000 a month) predates all coded weeks.
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Not averaged

claim_a: W8-L4: zinc-fortified soy protein dish base for public meals
claim_b: W8-L2: functional microbial feed ingredient for shrimp and pangasius
position_taken: Renumber one of them when the package is edited; this line refers to W8-L4's profile
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). ID clash between two wave 8 lines

topic: Scale of plant milk against dairy milk
claim_a: Kitchens: plant milks about 4.1% of milk litres on Kamereo; top plant SKU about 3% of the top dairy SKU (ECR-06)
claim_b: Consumer marketplaces: top plant SKU 60% (Lazada) and 79% (Tiki) of the top dairy SKU by litres (MKT-03; MKT-05)
position_taken: Both stand: different buyers. Households buy domestic nut and soy milks near dairy scale; cafes and restaurants buy dairy and a little imported oat
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Top-SKU ratios only; neither is a market share

claim_a: Plant powders are 2 of 25 powders and 1.7% of counters at WheyShop (ECR-08)
claim_b: On Lazada, 7 plant powder listings show 7,294 sales against 5,455 for 6 whey listings; the top plant listing is Vietnamese-made (MKT-03)
position_taken: Both stand; neither is representative. WheyShop counters are shop-set; Lazada rows are built from targeted queries
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Plant powder is a real online niche, but these data cannot size it

topic: Which soy milk brand leads online
claim_a: Tiki: Vinasoy Fami leads (27,855 cases for one SKU; Vinamilk soy milks at most 558) (MKT-05)
claim_b: Lazada: Vinamilk leads (14,800 cases of walnut soy milk; Vinasoy Store at most 1,600) (MKT-03)
position_taken: Both stand: platform-specific distribution; Metric's Shopee data (ECR-01) give Vinamilk 53.6% of liquid milk
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Do not read either platform as a brand share

topic: Whether e-commerce is only an incumbents' channel
claim_a: Wave 8: official brand stores take 84.7% of liquid-milk sales on Shopee, so e-commerce is an incumbents' channel, not a cheap launch route for a new brand (ECR-01; W8-L5)
claim_b: On Lazada, 99% of dry chay piece sales and 81% of frozen and chilled chay sales in our rows go through small specialist shops without official badges (MKT-03)
position_taken: Both stand: incumbents' channel for milks and processed meat; small-maker channel for chay dry goods
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Share figures are our calculation on the rows read

topic: Whether more than 10% imported textured soy breaks EU and UK origin for chay food preparations
claim_a: Wave 8 L3 (reading of XBA-30): more than 10% by weight of imported 2106 material makes a 2106.90 product non-originating
claim_b: EVFTA Protocol 1 Article 5(3)(a) (ORG-01) and the identical UK text: the tolerance is 10% of the weight of the product or ex-works price; on a value basis imported textured soy up to about 32 to 46% of weight passes (our calculation)
position_taken: The text allows weight or value; we treat the weight limit as the conservative case and the value reading as likely but unconfirmed
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Needs a MOIT or EU binding origin view; no T1 conclusion depends on it because isolate and gluten meet the rule anyway

topic: Whether the recipe condition binds for UK buyers
claim_a: Wave 8 L3: UKVFTA caps imported flour in dumplings at 20% and blocks chay preparations with more than 10% imported textured soy
claim_b: UK Trade Tariff (ORG-03; ORG-04): Vietnamese goods can claim UK-CPTPP, which needs only a change of chapter for 1902 (0% duty) and a change of subheading for 2106.90 (1.6% in 2026)
position_taken: For the UK the constraint is avoidable: at most a 1.6 point gap on chay preparations in 2026, none on dumplings
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Wave 8 noted the looser CPTPP rules but had not checked the CPTPP rates

topic: Wheat flour share in the Marks and Spencer prawn gyoza
claim_a: Open Food Facts estimated ingredient share: wheat flour about 8% (model estimate)
claim_b: Pack label: flour share not printed; tiger prawns 37% of the gyoza
position_taken: We use only printed percentages; the estimate is not evidence
notes: Version 0.4 (wave9, actor check and expansion). Estimates in crowd-sourced records are computed, not declared
